newsitem.title: USA: Starr denies Whitewater defendant's claim on deal.
newsitem.headline: Starr denies Whitewater defendant's claim on deal.

text.p: Whitewater prosecutors on Saturday denied offering probation rather than jail time to a former business partner of President Bill Clinton if she would give them evidence implicating him in illegal business deals.

Independent counsel Kenneth Starr, who leads the Whitewater probe, said in a statement he did not promise Susan McDougal any specific sentence for four fraud convictions she received in the first Whitewater trial in May.

But he did not deny McDougal's claims that she was offered a plea bargain deal and that investigators were solely interested in information implicating the president and first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton.

McDougal said on Friday she would not cooperate with Starr's team and would go to jail on Monday rather than accept a court order to testify before a grand jury on Clinton's alleged role in winning a fraudulent $300,000 loan in 1986.

"They are not people who want the truth. They don't want anything from me except what they can use against the Clintons," McDougal told CNN. She also said she had no knowledge of wrongdoing by the Clintons.
In his written response, Starr accused McDougal and her defence attorney of "outrageous and unethical" attempts to deceive the public.

He said he offered McDougal the "opportunity to voluntarily provide complete and truthful information about matters within the jurisdiction of this office," but that he did not promise to recommend a specific sentence to the judge in her trial.

She turned down the offer and was sentenced to two years in prison. After refusing to testify to the grand jury this week, McDougal was held in contempt of court and will receive more jail time on Monday unless she changes her mind.

Starr's team is investigating Clinton's personal and political finances. While the president has not been charged with any offence, several of his former allies and friends have been brought to trial.
Susan McDougal and her former husband James McDougal were business partners with the Clintons in the ill-fated Whitewater real estate venture.

James McDougal was found guilty on 18 fraud and conspiracy charges and faced up to 84 years in prison but has since decided to cooperate with prosecutors. It is not clear what information he might be able to give them on the Clintons.

Clinton testified in defence of the McDougals at the trial and flatly denied allegations that he twice pressured an Arkansas banker to give Susan McDougal a fraudulent $300,000 loan. Prosecutors said part of the money went to pay expenses of the Whitewater project.
